annuity-payout-calculator.assumptionNote: Assumes annual payouts at the end of each year and a constant annual return on the remaining balance.
benefits: Turns a lump sum into a concrete yearly and monthly income figure.
Shows how much of your payout stream is interest versus your own principal.
Helps you compare different payout horizons before committing.
Runs fully in your browser with no sign-up or data collection.

faqs.a: This calculator assumes a systematic withdrawal from an invested lump sum at a constant return. A real annuity contract from an insurer may guarantee the payout but includes fees and profit margins, so its payouts are usually lower than this model.
faqs.q: Is this the same as buying an annuity?

faqs.a: The classic 4% rule suggests withdrawing 4% of a retirement portfolio in the first year, adjusted for inflation, to make it last about 30 years. This calculator shows the exact sustainable payout for any horizon and return you choose.
A higher return supports a larger payout, but counting on high returns is risky. Use a conservative return, and remember this model assumes the rate never varies.
faqs.q: Should I use a high return to get a bigger payout?

faqs.a: Inflation erodes purchasing power, so a fixed nominal payout buys less each year. Real annuity contracts sometimes offer inflation-adjusted payouts at a lower starting amount; this tool models fixed nominal payouts.
Longer horizons mean smaller annual payouts from the same lump sum, because the money must stretch further. Try 20 versus 30 years to see the trade-off.
faqs.q: How does the payout period affect the payment?

faqs.a: Payouts from tax-deferred accounts are generally taxed as ordinary income. The tax treatment depends on your country and account type, which this calculator does not model.

annuity-payout-calculator.formula:
annual_payout = PV x r / (1 - (1 + r)^-n)
monthly_payout = annual_payout / 12
total_received = annual_payout x n
howTo: Enter the lump sum you want to convert into income.
Enter the expected annual return on the remaining balance.
Enter how many years the payouts should last.
Read your annual and monthly payout, the total received and the interest portion.
Adjust the horizon or return to compare scenarios.
keyFacts: An annuity payout converts a lump sum into a steady stream of payments over a chosen period.
Each payout partly returns your principal and partly pays out interest earned on the balance that is still invested.
A higher assumed return or a shorter payout period produces a larger annual payment.
The total you receive always exceeds the lump sum when the return is positive, because the unpaid balance keeps earning.
This is the reverse of the annuity savings calculation: instead of building a balance, you are drawing one down.
